clue.text: One operating a radio by means of cumbersome equipment at sea

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator
per means by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: An amateur radio enthusiast lugs bulky gear aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's hamper (as in 'top-hamper') is gear that is needed but gets in the way, especially rigging aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical usage, hamper is the necessary but encumbering gear of a vessel, such as spars and rigging.

clue.text: Individually produced, the servant said

indicators.note: said marks that the servant's word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: a handmaid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A maid remarks on bespoke craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods crafted by hand one at a time, not mass manufactured.

clue.text: Wind topples Communist base first

indicators.note: first says the word for base comes before the toppled word

parts.note: base means mean, low

indicators.note: topples in a down clue turns the word upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: A gale knocks over a Communist stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and turn, as a river does along its course.

clue.text: He will get out and run about over hill

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the earlier pieces above the hill

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat
C stands for circa, Latin for about
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A man escapes and runs off across the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: An extra is cricket's run not credited to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or person that draws something out, such as a fan removing fumes.

clue.text: Support someone at the bar

explanation.surface: Backing a person standing at the pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to back a cause; an advocate is also a barrister, a lawyer called to the bar.

clue.text: Lioness heeding order to be obstinate

indicators.note: order means the letters of the two words are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A lioness heeds a command only to turn stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to resist stubbornly and refuse to budge.

clue.text: Very loudly entering overbid

indicators.note: entering places the musical marking within the poetic word

parts.note: o'er is a poetic form of over
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone loudly outbidding at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid is an amount put forward to buy, a proposal of price.

clue.text: Passionate prophet encompasses our conversion

indicators.note: encompasses says the prophet's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

indicators.note: conversion changes the order of the three letters

explanation.surface: An ardent preacher seeks to convert us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' turns OUR into ROU, which 'encompasses' puts inside AMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of romantic or sexual desire, ardent in love.

clue.text: Australian stockade — I've found it!

explanation.surface: A discovery cried out at a fort in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eureka Stockade was an 1854 miners' revolt at Ballarat; the Greek exclamation is a cry of discovery.

clue.text: Ask me along if I'm involved in medicine

indicators.note: involved means the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A request to join in taking a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension of magnesium hydroxide taken as an antacid and laxative.

clue.text: Almost a disaster, discovering uranium missing

indicators.note: missing tells us the element's symbol is left out of the longer word

parts.note: discovering, as in digging something up, is unearthing
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A nuclear near-miss: some uranium has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, where disaster nearly happens, is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: The meal's the best part, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part, as in 'the flower of youth'

explanation.surface: Someone claims the meal is the highlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is ground grain, a synonym for powder milled from wheat.

clue.text: Lad wandering in the gloom, an urchin

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled boy's letters inside the word for darkness

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom

indicators.note: wandering suggests the three letters of lad roam out of order

explanation.surface: A boy roams lost in the darkness, a street child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes DLA from LAD, which 'in' puts inside MURK. A mudlark was a child scavenging on Thames riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark was a poor child who scavenged river mud for saleable scraps, hence a street child.

clue.text: It's known for jackets and not people

parts.note: nor means and not
folk means people

explanation.surface: A place famous for its jackets, not its inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: A Norfolk jacket is a belted tweed jacket; Norfolk is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk jacket, a loose belted country coat, takes its name from the English county.

clue.text: Ventured right inside the earth

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the word for soil

parts.note: dust means earth or soil

explanation.surface: Someone dared to go right into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past tense of dare, so it means dared or ventured.

clue.text: Firm head needed for this expedition!

parts.note: fast means firm, fixed
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: A trek that calls for a steady nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey but means speed, its older sense; FASTNESS can mean quickness as well as stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, which is also a sense of the answer, quickness.

clue.text: Russian chap lifted-gun before old Henry

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue raises the name so it reads upward, backwards

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
gat is slang for a gun
or is an archaic word for before, as in 'or ever'

explanation.surface: A Russian picks up a gun before an old king.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Henry the Navigator, a fifteenth-century Portuguese patron of voyages, is the 'old Henry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Henry of Portugal was nicknamed for his sponsorship of sea exploration.

clue.text: 15 blends or grains

indicators.note: blends means the letters are mixed together anew

explanation.surface: A mill mixing oats or grains.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is FASTNESS in its sense of stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold or fortified post, the place where troops are stationed.

clue.text: Lack a strand to hold a label

indicators.note: to hold means the beach word wraps round the label word

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A missing piece of thread to fasten a tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a deficiency or insufficiency of something needed.

clue.text: House transfer requires no old money

indicators.note: requires no means the penny symbol is dropped

parts.note: a handover is a transfer
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British currency

explanation.surface: A property sale that costs nothing in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: d is the old British penny, from Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal dynasty is a house; this one ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.

clue.text: It's the current number girl, is after

indicators.note: is after says the name follows the numeral

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals
Olga is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man counting off the girl he's chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is the flow of a river: the Volga is Russia's great river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current of water, and this is a major Russian river.

clue.text: Sweep employed by Charlotte Ryan

indicators.note: employed by means the letters are used within the two names

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep works for a woman named Charlotte Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is short for sweepstake, a prize draw.

clue.text: Second best part in hilarious performance

parts.note: the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: An actor plays a minor role in a comic show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely funny is informally called a riot or hoot.

clue.text: Move I cannot comprehend

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of the phrase around

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a chess move they cannot understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Comprehend in its older sense means include or hold within, as a box holds things.

clue.text: Bill has to deliver bitter

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
to rid is to free or deliver, as in 'deliver us from evil'

explanation.surface: Bill must hand over a pint of bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and pungent, harsh to taste or smell.

clue.text: Vessel less heavily laden

explanation.surface: A boat carrying a smaller load.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat barge for unloading ships; lighter also means weighing less.

clue.text: Fish always left inside

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the word for always

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A fish that is forever kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a small fish, the stage after migrating upriver.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing, with nothing on?

explanation.surface: A layabout lounging about naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy and lacking initiative; read whimsically, also lacking a shift, a slip or chemise, so unclothed.

clue.text: A red mini crashed at midday

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters of the small car are smashed into new order

explanation.surface: A red car came to grief at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Meridian means noon, the sun at its highest point.

clue.text: Drawing the line that curves round there

indicators.note: round turns the curved line's word back to front

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
yon is an old word for there, as in yonder

explanation.surface: Sketching a curving line around a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns ARC into CRA. A crayon can be a drawing done in crayon, as well as the stick itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made with coloured chalk or wax sticks is itself called by the tool's name.
